title: Scripts / CLI Bypass Audit v1
summary: 121 scripts with no unified taxonomy, no consistent dry-run default, no consistent schema validation boundary, no consistent auth model. Three critical bypass risks found. Only 3 scripts are properly gated (triple-flag confirmation for GitHub PR execution, dry-run default for auth check, read-only by design for security packet execution).

mutation_capable_scripts.recommendation: Gate all register/grant/revoke operations through governance engine. Dry-run by default. Require operator approval for non-dry-run.
Gate fleet start/stop/restart through governance engine. Dry-run by default.
Triple-flag gate properly implemented. Add governance spine call before allowing --execute-remote-mutation.

key_gaps: No unified command taxonomy — scripts use inconsistent flag names, output formats, and auth models
No consistent dry-run default — mutation scripts should default to dry-run but do not
No consistent schema validation boundary — some scripts emit structured JSON, others emit ad-hoc output
No consistent auth model — auth varies per-script (env vars, keychain, GitHub App auth, none)
Scripts bypass intent gating — the cockpit's intent system has no jurisdiction over scripts
Scripts can mutate without cockpit approval — no cross-surface approval path for script- initiated mutations
121 scripts with no discovery taxonomy — hard to audit which scripts exist and what they do
